literal: In the place where it does not work, anger is bad; even in the place where it works, there are no other things more evil than that.
translation: Anger is harmful when directed at those where it has no effect; even when directed at those where it does have an effect, there is nothing more evil than it.
modern: தன் கோபம் செல்லுபடியாகாத இடத்தில் கோபம் கொள்வது தீமையானது; தன் கோபம் செல்லுபடியாகும் இடத்திலும் அதைவிடத் தீமையானது வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet analyzes the consequences of anger in two distinct situations: against those who are stronger and against those who are weaker. In a situation where one's anger cannot prevail (against the powerful), harboring anger only causes self-harm and distress. Conversely, in a situation where one's anger does prevail (against the powerless), exercising it is the ultimate evil because it leads to oppression and moral ruin. Therefore, anger is entirely destructive and unjustifiable in any circumstance.
